name: Malbork
ground: A flat bank of the Nogat, chosen for the river rather than the height. Brick, because there is no building stone for a hundred miles and the clay is underfoot.

keep.name: The High Castle
keep.note: A closed quadrangle around a courtyard — a keep you can live an entire administration inside.

axis.name: The river frontage
axis.note: Seven hundred metres of brick along the water, which is the view, the wharf and the argument all at once.

figures.value: about 21 hectares — the largest castle in the world by area
the Teutonic Order, as a headquarters and not a fort

lesson: The largest castle in the world is made of the cheapest material available at the site. That is not a compromise, it is the reason it could be that large — a stone Malbork was never possible and a brick one was inevitable. Build with what is under your feet and the size takes care of itself.
